A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same iTool research. The main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original BFCL and API-Bank evaluations, component ablations, training-data analyses and preference-optimization experiments, including Appendix B.2.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including iTool's benchmark scores in Tables 1–3 and the appendix preference-optimization comparison.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same easy-to-hard warm-up, perplexity-based sampling, step-level MCTS preference construction and iterative SimPO optimization. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use ToolACE training data, the same BFCL scenarios and API-Bank L1/L2 evaluation tasks. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 1–3 and the ablations. Appendix B.2 retains the same DPO, SimPO, IPO and ORPO comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B retain the same training proportions, model configurations, accuracy metrics, checkpoint selection, training budgets and hyperparameter-search procedures.

E4.justification: The component, curriculum, MCTS, iteration-count, base-model and data-scaling analyses are retained. Appendix B.2's preference-algorithm analysis and Appendix C's cases also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains MCTS seed 42, and Figure 5 retains its existing error bars. No repeated-run information, uncertainty-reporting practice or significance-testing procedure changes.

E6.justification: The headline numerical comparison changes from approximately 3% over same-size models to approximately 12% over baseline models. All underlying table entries and plotted results remain unchanged: Table 3 still reports 62.92 for iTool, 60.44 for SFT and 50.15 for source Llama-3.1-8B. This is a revised comparison summary, not a measured performance improvement between versions.

T1.justification: The task formulation, Equations 1–11 and preference-objective formulas in Table 6 are unchanged. Neither version adds distinct theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and Introduction redefine the headline advantage from about 3% over same-size models to about 12% over baseline models. The methodological contributions and broader claims about competing with larger open- and closed-source models remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 7 removes the explicit qualification that computational parameter constraints may compromise performance. The computational burden, lack of validation on 30B/70B models, single-dataset limitation and other result interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the implementation settings, hardware, training time, filtering thresholds, prompts and software information. Section 7 still discloses seven hours on eight V100 GPUs per iteration; only its duplicate occurrence is removed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited-work membership are unchanged. Reference entries shift across pages without changes to research positioning.

P1.justification: Editing is limited to the headline performance sentences, shortening Section 7 and minor spacing. The section order, appendix organization and remaining narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 move from page 7 to page 6, and Table 1 gains blue highlighting for the iTool row. Existing figures and surrounding text are repositioned, especially across pages 6–8. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 slightly weakens qualification and clarity: Section 7 deletes the explicit possible performance cost of computational constraints, while the headline shifts from a same-size comparison to a larger 12% advantage over broadly described baselines without clarifying the intended contrast. Earlier placement of Tables 1–2 and reduced repetition modestly help presentation, but the unchanged supporting evidence does not resolve these reporting weaknesses.
